messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming.delivery p99 latency breached 5s in eu-west-1 for ~8m. Creating triage thread (1715943210). Paging oncall and SRE.
pri (incident-cmd): I'm on it, taking incident lead. Ana, mike — can you join? tagging @ana @mike
ana (sre): joining. I'm pulling logs & tracing for affected routes (/v1/chat/stream). Initial glance: a lot of SSE chunk gaps and edge proxy write timeouts around the same timestamps.
mike (eng-runtime): seeing sudden increase in tail token processing time and KV cache miss rate on the runtime nodes servicing eu-west-1. Also some `EPIPE` / `write timeout` entries from the edge-proxy.
liz (support): support has ~12 customers reporting streaming hangs where client UI shows "waiting for more" and then times out. I have a few session ids: sess_8f3, sess_9b2, sess_a11 — sending to ana in a DM.
jordan (prod-eng): can someone paste the proxy logs (errors) and a short representative request id? I want to correlate with runtime traces.
nana (sre): logging snippet:
```
2026-03-15T10:00:12Z edge-proxy[east-12]: 504 upstream timeout after 60000ms (req=rs_8f3)
2026-03-15T10:00:12Z runtime[east-3]: write EPIPE while sending chunk (req=rs_8f3)
2026-03-15T10:00:12Z edge-proxy[east-12]: sse flush interval exceeded, last_chunk=320ms
```
mike (eng-runtime): config note: default `proxy.stream.flush_interval_ms=200` and `proxy.write_timeout_ms=60000`. If clients stop reading (slow consumer), socket buffers back up and runtime sees blocked writes -> increased tail latency.
mike (eng-runtime): hypothesis: a subset of clients (or CDN nodes) are not consuming quickly, causing backpressure to propagate to runtime and the edge-proxy, leading to p99 spikes and chunking stalls.
net-ops-bot: Observability: increased retransmits and RTO spikes from CDN nodes in eu-west-1 starting 09:58Z. Packet loss ~0.6% on a subset of pop(s).
pri (incident-cmd): plan for immediate mitigation (short window): 1) enable smaller chunk flushing to avoid big writes; 2) increase proxy write timeout to avoid premature 504s while we stabilize; 3) enable slow-consumer soft-throttle on edge for affected routes; 4) open customer-facing note. Who can roll config?
mike (eng-runtime): I can push a config canary to edge-proxy. Will do incremental 5% → 25% → 100% if metrics look good. Proposed settings: `proxy.stream.flush_interval_ms=50`, `proxy.write_timeout_ms=120000`, enable `edge.throttle.slow_consumer=true`.
nana (sre): while canary runs I'll run correlation queries: p99 by route, by client ASN, and by connection window size. Sharing the query I used: `select p99(latency) from metrics where route='/v1/chat/stream' and region='eu-west-1' group by client_asn`
liz (support): drafting short customer msg now: "We're investigating streaming interruptions in EU, we've applied mitigations and will follow up with root cause." Will post to affected customers after we confirm mitigation reduces errors.
mike (eng-runtime): kicking off canary deploy: `deploy edge-proxy --canary 5 --set proxy.stream.flush_interval_ms=50 --set proxy.write_timeout_ms=120000 --set edge.throttle.slow_consumer=true`
mike (eng-runtime): deploy logs:
```
[10:03:22] triggering canary (5%)
[10:03:39] canary healthy: 120s healthchecks OK
[10:06:01] metrics: p99 (canary) 1.4s vs p99 (baseline) 5.9s
```
pri (incident-cmd): good sign. Ana, continue monitoring p95/p99 and chunking error rate. Liz, ready to send the customer note on my mark.
nana (sre): live metrics: after canary p99 for targeted route dropped from 6.2s -> 1.3s across canary nodes. Chunk gap rate decreased by ~78%. Correlating with the CDN ASNs — top impacted ASN(s): 12345, 67890.
net-ops-bot: net update: those ASNs show transient congestion between edge POP and CDN cluster at ~09:58-10:05Z, causing smaller TCP window and delayed ACKs.
liz (support): sending customer note now. Copy: "We observed transient streaming interruptions affecting some EU users between 09:58-10:10Z. We’ve applied mitigations (edge streaming flush and throttling) which reduced errors. We're continuing investigation and will follow up with RCA"
pri (incident-cmd): escalate to network team for follow-up with CDN partners on the ASN congestion. Opening post-incident RCA ticket: INF-2026-231. Assigning to jordan + net team + ana.
jordan (prod-eng): opened RCA ticket INF-2026-231 and added initial hypothesis + logs. Will schedule RCA sync tomorrow.
mike (eng-runtime): will leave the increased flush and write-timeout in place for the next 24h and roll back to previous values only after RCA confirms it's safe. I'll also add more granular metrics for client window size and per-conn backlog.
nana (sre): quick runbook note for oncall: if we see p99 > 3s and chunk-gap rate > 1% in eu-west-1 — enable flush_interval=50 and canary edge throttle. Steps recorded in incident runbook under "streaming slow consumer".
pri (incident-cmd): status update: mitigations deployed, customer notified, oncall monitoring. Handoff to follow-up team for RCA. If anything spikes back, page SRE lead.
nana (sre): current numbers (10:12Z): p95 0.4s (nominal), p99 1.2s (improved), error rate for streaming chunks down 0.02%.
liz (support): will follow up with the ~12 customers individually with session ids and offer logs/extra context.
pri (incident-cmd): marking this thread as handoff -> follow-up. Summary: cause likely network-induced slow consumers at CDN pop leading to backpressure + proxy timeouts; mitigation: smaller flush intervals & slow-consumer throttle + increased write timeout; next: RCA INF-2026-231. Thanks team — great quick coordination. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: Incident acknowledged as mitigated; monitoring continues. Incident status: UNDER INVESTIGATION -> MITIGATED (temporary).
-- end of thread --
